title: How test-negative influenza vaccine effectiveness studies make their methods choices: a scoping review to inform a regional protocol
subtitle: Scoping review of methods choices before a regional test-negative study
statement: The agency will run its own test-negative study of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness from the 2027 to 2028 season. Published estimates vary widely, probably because of methods choices such as case definition, test type, specimen timing, calendar-time adjustment, repeat testing, prior vaccination and, since 2020, the handling of SARS-CoV-2-positive controls. The protocol needs a map of how studies have made these choices.
whoAffected: The agency's epidemiologists and laboratories; sentinel practices; people in the region whose vaccination programme is judged on the estimates, including older adults in care homes.
whatHurts: Estimates that differ because of avoidable methods choices, leading to wrong messages about the vaccine.
currentPractice: The agency reports national estimates and has no local protocol.
whyNow: The protocol must be written by May 2027 for the 2027 to 2028 season.
constraints: One public health registrar for three months from January 2027; agency library access only; no contact with study authors beyond one email each; the map must be ready before the protocol is written in May 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: The region's vaccine effectiveness estimates are trustworthy enough to guide who is offered vaccination and how.
summary: Problem framed as a scoping review of methods choices.
